papers.title: Intervention Granularity Matters: Coherent Treatment Bundles in Counterfactual Simulation with Clinical World Models
papers.authors: Fangzhou Wang, Yixuan Yang, Camilla Balzarotti, Rishikesan Kamaleswaran
papers.summary: Clinical counterfactual world modeling changes coherent treatment bundles instead of independently editing variables, auditing treatment support in MIMIC-IV.
papers.use: A direct template for support-aware compound interventions in PerturbRx.
papers.steal: Define admissible intervention bundles and measure support before assessing counterfactuals.
papers.doubt: Does observational bundle coherence survive confounding and treatment-selection bias?

papers.title: Beyond Gaussian Worlds: Latent Geometry Matters for JEPAs
papers.authors: Léo Nicollier, Enric Meinhardt-Llopis, Marc Pic, Pablo Musé, Gabriele Facciolo
papers.summary: Examines how matching latent geometry, including spherical and toroidal targets, changes JEPA representation learning and identifiability.
papers.use: Useful for designing biological world-model latents beyond default Gaussian assumptions.
papers.steal: Ablate latent geometry while fixing encoder and evaluation protocol.
papers.doubt: Do theoretical assumptions hold in heterogeneous biological data, or is any gain merely stronger regularization?

papers.title: Available Guardrails: Certifying Selective Prediction across ML Systems
papers.authors: Parivesh Priye, Yufeng Wang, Haibin Ling, Michael Chaykowsky
papers.summary: Uses exact binomial certification and partitioned reporting to guarantee subgroup precision while quantifying finite-sample prediction availability.
papers.use: A rigorous bridge from Transfer Trust scores to actionable abstention policies.
papers.steal: Report subgroup precision lower bounds jointly with certified coverage.
papers.doubt: Does adaptive subgroup selection invalidate the guarantee, and does coverage collapse for rare groups?

papers.title: What Should We Ask Next? Retrieval-Aware Question Learning under Partial Evidence
papers.authors: Lyucheng Qian, John Yuehan Zhang, Pingyu Wang
papers.summary: RAVEL trains a question policy against downstream retrieval rank after the user's answer, rather than offline question discriminativeness.
papers.use: Transfers to active evidence gathering in scientific retrieval workflows.
papers.steal: Score questions by their effect on subsequent evidence retrieval.
papers.doubt: Can a person-retrieval objective transfer to biomedical evidence with unanswerable questions?

papers.title: Benchmarking World Models for Continual Learning on Compositional Tasks
papers.authors: Haoyu Zhou, Joe Watson, Anson Lei, Ingmar Posner
papers.summary: A compositional robot-manipulation curriculum separates reuse of learned perception/action factors from genuinely new learning.
papers.use: A transferable evaluation design for perturbation and context combinations.
papers.steal: Use separate splits for novel combinations of familiar factors and truly unseen factors.
papers.doubt: Are biological interactions sufficiently factorized, or would the proposed splits reward interpolation?

papers.title: World Modeling in Transformers
papers.authors: Pierre Beckmann, Matthieu Queloz, Andre Freitas
papers.summary: Causal interventions on TaxiGPT features distinguish internal map-like representations from reliable behavioral use.
papers.use: A falsification pattern for claims that a model learned a scientific world model.
papers.steal: Intervene on putative state features and test downstream prediction changes, beyond probes.
papers.doubt: Can the toy-environment intervention protocol scale to noisy biological states?

papers.title: LogicTrack: Auditing Reasoning Trajectories of Large Language Models with Formal Logic Solvers
papers.authors: Jingyu Hu, Shu Yang, Weiru Liu, Di Wang
papers.summary: Autoformalizes LLM reasoning steps for solver-based auditing and uses detected defects as backtracking feedback.
papers.use: Could audit reasoning paths in biomedical knowledge-graph answers.
papers.steal: Represent intermediate claims explicitly and score consistency separately from final-answer accuracy.
papers.doubt: Will autoformalization errors dominate, and does logical consistency correlate with scientific truth?

papers.title: DENSE: Distilling Agent Trajectories into Evidence-Grounded Shortcut Trees for Self-Refinement
papers.authors: Siyuan Liu, Fan Yu, Dongyu Ru, Yizhu Liu, Yifan Yang, Xuezhi Cao, Xunliang Cai, Yixin Cao
papers.summary: Compresses agent execution trajectories into reusable evidence-grounded shortcut trees; reports improved TerminalBench success and efficiency.
papers.use: A method for reusing verified research-agent search procedures.
papers.steal: Distill evidence-linked decision trees from full exploration traces.
papers.doubt: Could shortcut reuse miss novel counterevidence in scientific tasks?

papers.title: Time series generation with spectrally aligned latent flow matching
papers.summary: Adds Fourier, wavelet, and signature alignment to latent flow matching for time-series generation.
papers.use: A useful loss and diagnostic for longitudinal biomedical trajectories.
papers.steal: Evaluate generated trajectories by multiscale dynamics as well as pointwise fit.
papers.doubt: Spectral similarity may mask incorrect intervention responses or causal dynamics.

papers.title: MIST: Multimodal Survival Prediction with Genomic-Guided Histology Attention
papers.authors: Muhammet Sami Yavuz, Sabri Mustafa Kahya, Richard R. Chen, Jana Lipkova, Benedikt Wiestler
papers.summary: Genomic tokens guide attention over compact histology tokens for survival prediction, with missing-modality training and external cohort tests.
papers.use: Relevant to patient-context fusion and missing modalities, though not treatment response.
papers.steal: Use molecular context to select image evidence rather than pooling every patch equally.
papers.doubt: Survival association is not treatment effect; does robustness hold under site and modality-missingness shifts.
